items.prompt: In a notification preferences system, a notification gateway must deliver a user notification. a slow provider must not consume all request capacity The design review focuses on timeouts, deadlines, cancellation, and retry ownership. The normal path is healthy and the design must show where the decision belongs. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: a slow provider must not consume all request capacity
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is propagate the caller deadline and assign one retry owner with a bounded attempt budget..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Propagate the caller deadline and assign one retry owner with a bounded attempt budget. In this normal path for notification preferences, deadline propagation prevents work from outliving its user value; retry ownership prevents amplification. The owner must also make a dependency that times out intermittently observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide timeouts, deadlines, cancellation, and retry ownership independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a dependency that times out intermittently as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Propagate the caller deadline and assign one retry owner with a bounded attempt budget. It addresses a slow provider must not consume all request capacity through an explicit mechanism and keeps a dependency that times out intermittently inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Deadline propagation prevents work from outliving its user value; retry ownership prevents amplification. The applicability case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For notification preferences, the decision keeps a slow provider must not consume all request capacity attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a dependency that times out intermittently as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Timeouts, deadlines, cancellation, and retry ownership” to terminology recall. Distinguish protocol mechanics from domain boundaries; a fashionable API style is not automatically the correct contract. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce timeouts, deadlines, cancellation, and retry ownership must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.
